Definition: from G1909 and G875; to foam upon, i.e. (figuratively) to exhibit (a vile passion):--foam out.
BiblicalUsage: Epaphrizo means to foam out, and Jude uses it once, of false teachers foaming out their own shame like wild waves of the sea. The picture is ugly on purpose: what is inside them spills out for everyone to see.
TheologicalSignificance: What a person foams out reveals what is really inside them, and Jude warns us to look at the fruit, not the fine words.
